extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures. Unlike existing benchmarks, MMMU focuses on advanced perception and reasoning with domain-specific knowledge, challenging models to perform tasks akin to those faced by experts.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, common university majors were reviewed to decide what subjects should be included, based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted. 30 subjects from six different disciplines were selected. In the second stage, over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to assist in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. They were also advised to select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination concerns. This process resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions from various sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control involved two steps. First, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed and eliminated by authors. Second, problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. Finally, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% of 'very easy' problems were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A comprehensive protocol was used for annotating the dataset. Annotators were instructed to ensure all questions contained one or more images, were written in English, met college-level difficulty, and were unambiguous. Each question was categorized as multiple-choice or open-ended. All fields were annotated, including question text, answer options (for multiple-choice), correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Images were inserted as file paths within the question/options/explanations. A secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence, and regular audits of random samples were conducted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification was developed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for a detailed review process and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized approach for annotation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in various majors.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The live-updating leaderboard is available at: https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard. The paper includes a Version Change Log (Appendix J) detailing updates to results and model names, implying ongoing maintenance and updates.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is designed to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which is defined as an AI system reaching 'at least 90th percentile of skilled adults' in a broad range of tasks. This could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption, making it of both intellectual and societal importance to monitor. The benchmark aims to stimulate the development of next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. However, strong performance on this benchmark is argued to be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It measures three essential skills in LMMs: perception, knowledge, and reasoning, aiming to assess how well models can perceive and understand information across different modalities and apply reasoning with subject-specific knowledge to derive solutions. It is intended to be instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI.
